title: TB diagnosis as an encyclopedia index
dek: Wikipedia's diagnosis-of-tuberculosis page is a menu of test names. WHO mWRD-first grammar stays on tb-diagnosis.
story: Wikipedia's Diagnosis of tuberculosis article is a list: smear, culture, NAAT, IGRA, imaging, LAM. Useful as an index of names. Dangerous as a sequence, because it will not consistently put a WHO-recommended rapid molecular test first.
Simplfy's tb-diagnosis plate is the programme spine. This card exists so searches for the encyclopedia title land on that spine via related[].
Mixing infection tests into a disease-diagnosis list is the usual Wikipedia drift. Keep TST/IGRA on their own nodes.
deep: Pediatric stool WRD and urine LAM are clinic-module objects.
Do not treat a 'list of tests' as Bayesian updating — see stats predictive-value plates for that math.
Culture remains the DST workhorse even when NAATs front the door.

visual.caption: Encyclopedia index of names, then the WHO-shaped split Simplfy actually uses: disease diagnostics versus infection tests.
